handback.t:
TEAM A status: highest round R114 (R107-R114 done this stretch). Main HEAD 7319087, local commits only, no push. `cargo test --release --lib` = 401 pass. The 4 encoder tests that don't need weights pass; the weight-dependent one passes only with NM_ENCODER_WEIGHTS set. Without it, the default `cargo test` prints SKIP and doesn't exercise the model.

**Team B integrated, all cherry-picked clean:**
- 549ed7d (B36-B37)
- 07c8923 (B38-B39; B38 is a negative, so only B39 code landed)
- 2fa76b1 (B40-B42)
- afb40f1 (B43-B50)
- Only src/store.rs, src/bin/meshstore.rs, RD-LOG-B.md and the small py/b*.py scripts came in; no results/ blobs.

**Kept:**
- **R108, tie re-count of older quant rounds (CONFIRMED).** `py/b1/lib.py` now counts ties and has a `TP=1` mode where a tie for top counts as a miss. I recomputed the f32 baseline under the same rule (0 ties).
  - R9 int8, R10 f16, R13 PCA192 f32, R14a/b/c PCA+int8: 0 top ties and 0 rank ties. Every kept verdict is unchanged to the printed precision.
  - R11 int4: 25/22,229 rank ties; verdict unchanged.
  - **R12 binary sign was tie-inflated:** 1.4% of top-1 decisions and 35% of relevant-doc ranks were tied. Under the strict rule it has 15 Holm-significant losses instead of 11. It was already REJECTED, and that verdict now stands more strongly.
- **R109, formal Holm + TOST of Rust-encoder retrieval equivalence (CONFIRMED).** 24 cells over 2 corpora, 3 metrics and 2 halves, vs the stored ORT query vectors. 0 Holm-significant differences, max |d| .0031, and all 24 cells equivalent within ±.01 (max Holm-adjusted TOST p .026).
- **R110, encoder unit tests.** The gelu mutation check fails both the erf/gelu test and the weight test.
- **R111-R112, the main efficiency win.**
  - **Cause:** a profile showed the scalar activation quantiser took 60% of the int8 encoder time, and it ran 3 times on the same input for Q/K/V.
  - **Fix:** an AVX2 quantiser shared by Q/K/V (int8 encoder 2.2x faster), plus an AVX512-VNNI int8 kernel.
  - **VNNI kernel:** the portable AVX2 fallback is kept, and the VNNI path is bit-identical to AVX2 (unit test plus whole-encoder embeddings).
  - **Speed:** 10.2 → 3.2 ms/query single-thread bs=1, about 3.2x overall. Int8 is now faster than f32 in every config; it was slower in R104.
  - **Parity:** the new rounding is not identical to the old int8, so I re-checked. Mean cosine to ORT is .9971, MRR is unchanged, and 23 of 24 equivalence cells hold.
  - **Exception:** B int8 hit@5, CONF half, is inconclusive (TOST Holm p .059; 4 discordant queries), not negative.
- **R114, quiet-box end-to-end re-measure (CONFIRMED).** Box load was 3-5% and two runs agree within about 10-15%, so the absolutes are reported as measured. The pure-Rust text → encoder → int8 hybrid search_fast lookup takes 3.7 ms single-thread for one query. The best case is 2.9 ms (int8, 4 threads, bs=16). R106 measured 16.3 ms single-query and 5.4 ms best case on a loaded box. Top-1 is the source paragraph in 294/300 in every config.
  - The lookup half is now about 0.6 ms for 12-word queries.
  - The encoder is now 3-5x the lookup instead of 10-17x.
  - These queries average 20 tokens, so they are not comparable to short-query numbers.

**Rejected / honest negatives:**
- **R107:** the first re-measure of R106 was NOT on a quiet box (30-37% CPU from other processes), so I deferred absolutes there; R114 later settled it.
- **R113:** on identical prompts the Rust int8+VNNI encoder is still 1.7x (1 thread, bs=1) to 2.7x (4 threads, bs=16) slower than ORT int8. R104/R106 said about 3x slower, so the gap narrowed. ORT stays the faster encoder when python is acceptable.
- Rust f32 is still 2.1x slower than ORT fp32 at bs=1.

**Next list (R115+):**
- Persistent thread pool instead of per-layer `thread::scope`; 4 threads give only ×1.2-1.45.
- Fuse activation quantise into LayerNorm/GELU.
- Pre-packed VNNI weight layout and int8 attention.
- Add AVX-VNNI-256 for Intel cores; I tested only Zen 4.
- Re-run the R104 ORT comparison.
- Pool the R109 halves if hit@5 equivalence needs more power.
